summary: Author a fictional world whose invented rule set is stated and consistently enforced, so travel between islands has real constraints.
objective: Build a floating island world with declared wind currents and anchor points where a glider can travel between islands under stated rules.
intent_signals: Build a world of floating islands I can travel between.
Design a sky world with wind currents that actually affect movement.
example_prompts: Build a floating archipelago with updrafts, anchor lines and a glider I can pilot between islands.
Design a fictional sky world whose rules for staying aloft are stated and enforced.
negative_signals: Not an aerodynamics simulation: lift here follows an authored rule set, not aerofoil physics.
Not a geological or meteorological model of any kind.
not_for: Not an aerodynamics simulation: lift here follows an authored rule set, not aerofoil physics.
Not a geological or meteorological model of any kind.

entities.name: Island bodies
entities.guidance: Give each island a top surface, an eroded underside and a visible root or crystal mass, so the invented buoyancy has a stated cause.

entities.name: Wind field
entities.guidance: Author currents as named volumes with direction and strength, visible when a wind overlay is enabled, since travel depends on them.

entities.name: Glider and anchors
entities.guidance: Build a glider with a real wing, a pilot position and anchor lines that attach to island mooring points with a stated maximum length.

state_contract.model: World rule set stating what keeps islands aloft and how wind volumes affect a glider, plus glider position, velocity, altitude and anchor state. The rules are fictional but fixed and enforced everywhere.
state_contract.authority: The declared rule set is authoritative and applies to every object in the world. An island that floats for a different reason than the rules state is a world inconsistency, not a decoration.
actions: Launch the glider and ride an updraft.
Attach and release an anchor line at a mooring point.
Reset the glider to the launch platform.

invariants: The stated levitation rule applies to every island, including background ones.

In unanchored free flight the glider loses altitude outside an updraft and gains it inside one. Anchoring, landing and surface collision take precedence over wind, so a moored or landed craft does not sink because it is outside a current.

An anchor can only be attached to a mooring within line reach, and once attached the line never exceeds its declared length; if the tether constraint and a rock collision cannot both be satisfied the scene freezes and reports the conflict rather than letting the craft penetrate the island.
motion_guidance: Drive the glider with bounded acceleration from wind and gravity, and let the pilot pose respond to turns.
Animate cloud layers and streamers at different heights so altitude change is readable without a numeric display.
known_limits: Fictional world rules: nothing here is a physical claim about buoyancy, air density or flight.
Anchor lines are constraints, not simulated ropes with mass and stretch.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

object_craft.structure: Layered top soil, exposed rock face and an eroded underside with dangling roots or crystal spires that vary per island.
object_craft.material: Grounded natural families on top with a distinct luminous or crystalline treatment on the underside, so the fantasy element is localised rather than global.
object_craft.articulation: Islands are static; only the glider, lines and vegetation move.

object_craft.structure: Wing with visible spars and fabric, a harness and a pilot with weight-shift posture, plus a coiled line and hook.
object_craft.material: Fabric and timber materials so the craft reads as buildable within the world, avoiding a generic metallic look.
object_craft.articulation: The glider banks with turn rate and the pilot shifts weight; the anchor line follows a constrained curve between hook and mooring.

object_craft.structure: Streamer particles and drifting cloud sheets that follow the authored current volumes.
object_craft.material: Semi-transparent streamers that never obscure the horizon line; the overlay uses a legend with direction and strength.
object_craft.articulation: Streamers advect along their current volume and are recycled at the boundary.

physical_contract.scope: Authored glider steering influenced by declared wind volumes and an anchor constraint; no aerodynamics or rope dynamics.
colliders: Glider bounds against island surfaces and mooring structures.
driving: Wind volume contribution plus gravity, with bounded turn rate and pitch authority.
contact: Landing on a surface stops descent; collisions with rock faces stop forward motion instead of penetrating.
checks: In unanchored free flight, altitude falls outside updraft volumes and rises inside them; anchoring, landing and surface collision take precedence as declared.
Anchor length is never exceeded during any manoeuvre.

creative_affordances: The levitation rule is yours to invent: buoyant mineral, tethered spirits or an ancient machine all work if applied consistently.
Travel can be by glider, balloon or rope bridges; only the enforcement of the rules must stay constant.
